          NWSL Play-Off Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer Projections for the 2026 Championship
        
      
                          
                      Nov 5, 2026
          
                      Louise Beltrame-Bawden / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
The 2026 NWSL play-offs have arrived. Who will lift the inaugural Championship title? We provide our Opta supercomputer predictions.
The 2026 NWSL Play-offs have arrived, bringing with them another fiercely contested battle for the Championship.

Following our end-of-season projections, the Opta supercomputer has, for the first time, simulated the play-off bracket to estimate each team's chances of lifting the trophy and being crowned NWSL champions.
Gotham FC head into the post-season as slight favourites, but San Diego Wave are close behind. Kansas City Current and Washington Spirit remain firmly in the mix.
With eight teams in pursuit of one title, who will emerge as the 2026 NWSL champions?
Gotham have already made history this season. Now, they have their sights set on something even bigger.

Having secured their first-ever NWSL Shield with a 2-0 victory over Utah Royals on Decision Day, Gotham enter the play-offs looking to complete a historic double and defend the Championship they won in 2025.

Strengthened by the summer arrivals of former Chelsea stars Sam Kerr and Guro Reiten, Gotham have assembled a formidable squad. Should they go all the way, they would become the first side since North Carolina Courage in 2018 and 2019 to win back-to-back Championships.
They would also join North Carolina and Orlando Pride among the clubs to have won the Shield and Championship in the same season. But can they do it?

According to the supercomputer, Gotham have a 21.2% probability of lifting the trophy, making them marginal favourites in what promises to be one of the most competitive post-season battles in recent memory.
San Diego Wave are close behind on 20.4%, followed by Kansas City Current (18.0%) and Washington Spirit (14.3%). Indeed, just 6.9 percentage points separate the four leading contenders.
Interestingly, while Gotham are the most likely champions, they are not the team with the best chance of reaching the final.

That distinction belongs to San Diego Wave, who have a 41.4% probability of reaching the Championship game, narrowly ahead of Gotham (39.5%). Kansas City (31.4%) and Washington (30.3%) who complete the leading quartet.
Among the chasing pack, Angel City have a 9.3% chance of winning their first Championship, followed by Portland Thorns (7.6%), Seattle Reign (5.0%) and Utah Royals (4.2%).
With no team given even a one-in-four chance of lifting the trophy, the supercomputer suggests there could be plenty of twists and turns before the champions are crowned.
But first, eight teams must navigate four quarter-final encounters. So, who does the supercomputer favour in each matchup?

San Diego Wave enter their quarter-final against Utah Royals as the strongest favourites of the opening round. The Opta supercomputer gives them a 57.7% probability of victory in 90 minutes, compared to 20.4% for Utah, with a draw playing out in 22.0% of simulations.
History favours San Diego, who have won all six previous meetings between the sides, making Utah the only NWSL opponent against whom they boast a perfect record.
Indeed, the Wave are one of just two teams, along with Kansas City, that Utah has not won a point against since returning to the NWSL in 2024.

Jonas Eidevall’s side also arrive in electric form, unbeaten in seven matches (W6 D1), their longest such run in club history. Their 1.93 points per match this season is also a club record, surpassing their Shield-winning campaign in 2023 (1.68).
